implementation_notes: The composition engine is in the standard library: each fragment is a {{define "name"}} template, inserted with {{template "name" .}} ({{block}} adds a default that a page may override), and template.ParseFS/ParseGlob loads a directory of fragment and page files into one namespace with html/template providing context-aware escaping. This replaces hand-written page assembly; pass each fragment a narrow struct as its data (the . argument) instead of reaching into a shared map, and note that {{template}} executes against the data you give it - the caller, not the fragment, is the View Manager.
pitfalls: Templates parsed into the same set share the func map and delimiters, but ParseFiles/ParseGlob create a new root template each call - fragment definitions must be part of the set you execute, and files sharing a base name override earlier ones in parse order.
html/template's contextual escaping is defeated by template.HTML/template.JS values injected to smuggle pre-rendered fragments; keep raw-markup values out of fragment data.
Passing a fragment the page-level struct (the whole .) instead of its own narrow data couples every fragment to the page shape and makes reuse across pages impossible.
